# Molding with Integrated Electrode Pattern and Manufacturing Method

## Object of the Invention

The present invention aims to provide a molding with an integrated electrode pattern in which a band-shaped second film containing an electrical connecting portion can be securely fixed to the inner surface of a resin molded body. This configuration ensures reliable positioning and stable retention of the second film, thereby improving both the electrical integrity and the mechanical durability of the resulting product.

## Structure of the Invention

The molding is constructed from a resin molded body upon which multiple functional films are integrated. A first film is formed on the inner surface of the resin molded body. This first film includes an electrode pattern, together with a first lead-out wire that is electrically connected to that electrode pattern. In this way, the first film provides the primary electrode functionality along with a means for electrical connection.

In addition, a band-shaped second film stands on the inner surface of the resin molded body. This second film includes a second lead-out wire, which is electrically connected to the first lead-out wire of the first film. Through this arrangement, electrical continuity is established between the two films, allowing signals or power to be transmitted across the integrated structure.

To ensure the secure fixation of the second film, the resin molded body features a pair of support wall portions. These support wall portions are formed integrally with the inner surface of the resin molded body and stand upright so as to clamp both ends of the base part of the second film. By holding the base part of the second film from both sides, the support wall portions maintain the second film in an upright, stable position and prevent unwanted displacement or detachment.

## Manufacturing Method

The invention further encompasses a method for manufacturing this molding with an integrated electrode pattern. This manufacturing method provides a systematic process for forming the resin molded body together with the first film, the band-shaped second film, and the integrally formed support wall portions, thereby producing a molding in which the electrode pattern and the associated electrical connecting portions are reliably integrated.

# Molding with Integrated Electrode Pattern

## Technical Background

This patent addresses a significant challenge in the manufacture of molded articles incorporating electrical functionality: the secure fixation of a band-shaped second film containing an electrical connecting portion to the inner surface of a resin molded body. In conventional approaches, films bearing electrode patterns and their associated wiring have often suffered from insufficient mechanical stability when integrated into resin structures, particularly at the points where electrical connections must be maintained with external components. This instability can compromise both the physical integrity of the assembly and the reliability of its electrical performance over time.

## Summary of the Invention

The present invention solves this problem through a molding with an integrated electrode pattern that combines two distinct film components. The first film bears the electrode pattern and a corresponding lead-out wire, forming the primary functional surface of the structure. Coupled to this is an upright second film, which contains a connected second lead-out wire that establishes the electrical pathway between the internal electrode pattern and the external environment. The second film is arranged in an upright orientation, allowing it to extend away from the plane of the first film and toward the point of external connection.

## Key Innovation

The central innovation of this patent lies in the provision of a pair of support wall portions formed integrally with the resin molded body. These support walls are configured to clamp both ends of the base part of the second film, securing it firmly in position. By gripping the second film at both ends of its base, the integrated support walls hold the film in its upright orientation without reliance on separate fasteners or adhesives that might degrade or loosen over time.

## Advantages

This clamping arrangement significantly improves the mechanical stability of the assembly. The band-shaped second film, which carries the electrical connecting portion, is held rigidly against displacement, vibration, and mechanical stress. As a direct consequence of this enhanced physical stability, the electrical connection between the film and external substrates becomes more reliable and consistent. The integrated formation of the support wall portions with the resin molded body also streamlines manufacturing, as the fixation structure is created as part of the molding process itself, eliminating the need for additional assembly steps or components.

In summary, by uniting the first and second films into a single molded structure and securing the second film through integrally formed clamping support walls, the invention achieves a robust and dependable means of connecting internal electrode patterns to external substrates.

# The Object and the Solution

Every problem begins with an object—something concrete or abstract that captures our attention and demands understanding. The object might be a broken machine, a mathematical equation, a strained relationship, or a business challenge. Whatever form it takes, the object represents the starting point of any meaningful inquiry.

## Understanding the Object

Before we can act, we must first examine the object closely. What is its nature? What conditions surround it? The object is never truly isolated; it exists within a web of circumstances that shape its behavior and its meaning. A skilled thinker learns to observe the object from multiple angles, resisting the temptation to jump immediately toward conclusions.

The way we perceive the object often determines how we approach it. Two people may look at the same object and see entirely different things—one sees an obstacle, another sees an opportunity. This subjective dimension reminds us that objects are not merely passive things; they are interpreted through the lens of human experience.

## Arriving at the Solution

The solution emerges from our engagement with the object. It is the resolution, the answer, the path forward that transforms confusion into clarity. But a solution is rarely obvious at first glance. It requires patience, creativity, and sometimes a willingness to fail before succeeding.

The best solution is not always the most complicated one. Often, simplicity holds the greatest power. When we strip away unnecessary complexity, we frequently discover that the solution was hidden within the object all along, waiting to be revealed.

## The Connection Between Them

What binds the object and the solution together is the process of thought and effort that connects them. The journey from problem to answer is where genuine learning happens. In the end, understanding this relationship—between the object we face and the solution we seek—is one of the most valuable skills a person can develop.

counterfactuals.output:
# Patent Abstract

## Molding with Integrated Electrode Pattern

**Abstract**

A molding having an integrated electrode pattern and a method for producing the same, wherein an electrically conductive electrode structure is embedded within or applied to a molded substrate body to form a unified component suitable for capacitive sensing, heating, illumination control, or signal transmission applications.

---

### Object of the Invention

The object of the present invention is to provide a molding with an integrated electrode pattern that overcomes the limitations of conventional assemblies in which electrode structures are attached to a substrate as separate components. Existing solutions suffer from poor adhesion, delamination under thermal or mechanical stress, increased assembly complexity, higher production costs, and limited freedom in forming three-dimensional or curved electrode geometries. A further object is to achieve reliable electrical performance while maintaining a compact, durable, and aesthetically seamless component that can be manufactured in high volumes with consistent quality.

---

### Solution

The stated object is achieved by a molding in which an electrode pattern is integrally formed with a molded base body during or in conjunction with the molding process. According to the invention, an electrically conductive material is arranged in a predetermined pattern and at least partially encapsulated by, or bonded to, a moldable resin such that the electrode structure and the substrate form a single cohesive unit.

In a preferred embodiment, the electrode pattern is provided on a carrier film that is inserted into a mold cavity and back-molded (in-mold or insert molding) with a thermoplastic or thermosetting material, thereby fixing the electrode geometry relative to the molded body. Alternatively, the conductive pattern may be deposited, printed, or plated onto a preformed molding surface and subsequently secured by an overmolded protective layer.

This construction provides robust mechanical anchoring of the electrodes, eliminates separate mounting steps, enables complex two- and three-dimensional electrode layouts on planar or curved surfaces, and yields a sealed, durable component with reliable and reproducible electrical characteristics.

# Patent Abstract

## Resin Molded Body with Secured Band-Shaped Film for External Substrate Connection

**ABSTRACT**

A resin molded body is provided that securely fixes a band-shaped film having electrical connection functionality to an external substrate. The resin molded body comprises a molded resin base portion and a band-shaped film at least partially embedded within or fixed to the resin base portion. The band-shaped film includes a plurality of electrical wiring patterns formed thereon and a connection terminal region extending outward from the resin base portion for electrical coupling to the external substrate. 

To achieve secure fixation and prevent detachment or positional displacement, the resin base portion includes an anchoring structure that engages the band-shaped film. In one aspect, the anchoring structure comprises a resin retaining portion that surrounds at least one edge of the band-shaped film, wherein a portion of the resin flows through one or more through-holes or engagement openings formed in the band-shaped film during molding, thereby forming an integral mechanical lock. This configuration suppresses stress concentration at the connection terminal region and maintains stable electrical continuity between the band-shaped film and the external substrate even under thermal cycling, vibration, or external mechanical load.

The band-shaped film may be a flexible printed circuit (FPC) or flexible flat cable, and the connection terminal region may be configured for soldering, press-fitting, or connector-based coupling to the external substrate. The resulting resin molded body provides improved reliability of electrical connection, enhanced mechanical durability, and simplified assembly to external electronic devices.

---

*Note: This is a sample abstract template. For an actual patent filing, the specific structural features, materials, and connection methods should be tailored to your particular invention and reviewed by a qualified patent attorney.*

# Technical Abstract

## Resin Molded Structure with Integrated Electrode Patterns and Lead-Out Wires

**Abstract**

A resin molded structure (10) is disclosed comprising a first film (12) having an electrode pattern (14) and lead-out wires (16) formed on a surface thereof, wherein said first film (12) is integrally embedded within a resin molding (20) formed by injection molding. The electrode pattern (14) is electrically connected to the lead-out wires (16), which extend toward a peripheral region (18) of the resin molded structure (10) for external electrical connection.

A second film (22) is disposed in opposing relation to the first film (12), wherein a plurality of support wall portions (24) project from an inner surface of the resin molding (20) and are configured to clamp the second film (22) therebetween. The support wall portions (24) maintain a predetermined spacing (S) between the first film (12) and the second film (22), thereby defining an internal gap region (26) that protects the electrode pattern (14) from deformation during the resin injection process.

Each support wall portion (24) includes a clamping surface (28) that engages a peripheral edge (30) of the second film (22), preventing displacement of the second film (22) due to injection pressure of molten resin (32). The lead-out wires (16) are routed through a channel (34) defined between adjacent support wall portions (24), ensuring electrical continuity while maintaining structural isolation from the flowing resin (32).

In a preferred embodiment, the first film (12) and the second film (22) comprise a thermoplastic resin material, and the electrode pattern (14) is formed from a conductive silver paste or printed conductive ink. The resin molding (20) encapsulates and protects the integrated components, providing a durable, low-profile assembly suitable for capacitive touch sensors, in-mold electronic devices, and human-machine interface applications.

- **24** — support wall portions
- **26** — internal gap region
- **28** — clamping surface
- **30** — peripheral edge
- **32** — molten resin
- **34** — channel
- **S** — predetermined spacing
